source:
@@U00154@@
Useless! What do you open? You were my keys. I stood at the gates panting with expectation, but you unlocked nothing. Even in the sun’s uncompromising light Nature remains a mystery. Demure, chaste, she lifts no veil. Nothing. And you, 浮士德, with your levers and screws, are impotent in the face of Nature; as impotent as these ancient instruments I’ve never used: my father’s tools, grimy, gathering soot from my smoking lamp. What a fool. I should have squandered the little I had, rather than waste my life under the weight of this! To own what the past has left, you must use it. Not to is a terrible burden. Only what the moment creates can serve the moment.

@@U00155@@
(He sees a flask on a shelf.)

@@U00156@@
That flask— why does it draw my eye like a magnet? It clears my mind like moonlight suddenly flooding a dark forest. Come, come down, you rarest, you holiest of vials! I praise the human cunning that made you, you distillation of sleep-inducing herbs, quintessence of subtle poisons!
translation:
@@U00154@@
没用！你打开什么？你是我的钥匙。我站在门口气喘吁吁地期待着，但你什么也没打开。即使在阳光下，大自然仍然是一个谜。她端庄、贞洁，不摘面纱。没有什么。而你，浮士德，你的杠杆和螺丝，在大自然面前是无能为力的；就像这些我从未使用过的古老工具一样无能：我父亲的工具，肮脏不堪，积聚着我冒烟的灯里的烟灰。真是个傻瓜。我应该挥霍我所拥有的一点点，而不是在这样的重压下浪费我的生命！要拥有过去留下的东西，你必须使用它。不这样做是一个可怕的负担。只有当下创造的东西才能为当下服务。

@@U00155@@
（他看到架子上有一个烧瓶。）

@@U00156@@
那个烧瓶——为什么它像磁铁一样吸引着我的目光？它让我的思绪变得清晰，就像月光突然淹没了黑暗的森林。来吧，下来吧，你这个最稀有、最神圣的瓶子！我赞扬人类的狡猾，正是它们使你——催眠草药的精华——微妙毒药的精髓！
